subject: Mid-quarter pulse: perf OKR re-scope + cross-pod dependency asks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-quarter pulse: perf OKR re-scope + cross-pod dependency asks

Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse and a proposed narrower scope for the performance OKR so we can hit an impactful milestone before QBR. TL;DR: request we trim the OKR to focus on 1) 95th percentile decoding latency (-20% target) for the 8k path for the public hosted footprint, and 2) a canary rollout plan across two customer segments.

Why: we’re behind on several items that drive latency unit cost (kv-cache locality, kernel selection for 8k, and batching behavior for interactive endpoints). Given limited engineering runway, a focused win on the 8k path gets us measurable unit-cost improvements and a clear metric for the QBR.

Asks by pod (please reply with commitment + blocking items by EOD Wed):
- Infra (Karthik / Neha): confirm Dedicated pool reservation for a weekend canary (2x A100 equiv) and whether we can enable the new kernel selector flag on staging without infra-wide risk. Also need a short-lived quota for parallel canaries.
- Serving/runtime (Karthik): quick triage on the kv-cache locality regression (SUP-1234) — we need a mitigation path or a rollback.
- Product (Laura): accept the trimmed OKR and sign off on the customer segments for canary (Tier1: 5 early adopters, Tier2: internal Beta). Also confirm we can push a short customer communication draft by next Tue.
- Research/Applied ML (Sergio): finalize quantization profile recommendation for the 8k path (see attached quantization-plan-v1.md) and provide perf delta estimates for int8 quant vs bf16.

I attached a one-pager with the proposed trimmed OKR and the minimal success criteria — please read before replying. If anyone thinks we should keep additional subgoals (e.g., rep-rate improvements, embedding drift checks), call it out but include the expected incremental effort.

I’ll collate replies and propose a revised OKR doc for exec review on Thu.

Thanks —
Vanessa
VP, Platform Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-09-27_midq_pulse_one-pager.pdf (PDF), quantization-plan-v1.md (text)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter pulse: perf OKR re-scope + cross-pod dependency asks

Vanessa — thanks for the clear ask. Quick status and blockers: 

1) Dedicated pool reservation: we can reserve capacity for a weekend canary but need a signed short-term PO from Finance (I’ll loop in procurement). Estimated cost ~ $9k for the weekend if we do 2x A100 equiv.

2) Kernel selector flag on staging: we can flip the flag on staging today; however, there is one outstanding failure mode where longer sequences (>6k) can OOM under the new selector because of a prefetch path. I captured the detail in SUP-1234. Mitigation options:
   - Fast rollback toggle (works, low risk) — 1 day to test; OR
   - Patch the prefetch window (safer but ~3 days).

3) kv-cache locality regression (SUP-1234): confirmed there is an allocation pattern change from the last runtime refactor that reduces locality for some workloads. I can assign an engineer to a hotfix but it’ll be a focused 3-day effort. Without it, the measured latency improvement from kernel changes is muted.

Commitment: I can own the weekend canary infra reservation (conditional on PO) and assign one engineer to the kv-cache hotfix starting Wed. If we choose the rollback toggle route, we can proceed with canary this Friday.

I’ll open the SUP ticket with the rollback plan and link the canary runbook.

-Karthik
Director, Infrastructure

Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1234

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter pulse: perf OKR re-scope + cross-pod dependency asks

Agree with the narrowed scope. A few notes from product side: 

- Canary customer list: I propose the 5 early adopters be: AcmeHealth, NovaClaims, BeaconFin, EchoAssist, and internal Beta accounts (we already have non-prod test tenants). I’ll start outreach to AcmeHealth — Maria is ok with experimental canaries as long as we give 48h heads up.
- Customer comms: we’ll use a short incident-style template (1 paragraph, expected impact, timeframe, opt-out link). I can produce a first draft by Mon 10/4.
- Success criteria: set the QBR metric to 95th pctl latency for 8k requests dropping by >=15% in canary and >=20% by post-rollout (to leave a bit of buffer).

Constraints: we’ll need the kv-cache hotfix or the rollback toggle before we do any external canary — internal Beta is fine without it. We also need legal review on the comms for AcmeHealth (Maria will loop legal on their side).

Timeline that I can commit to if infra confirms PO and rollback option:
- Wed 9/29: infra confirms flag + rollback plan (Karthik)
- Fri 10/1: internal Beta canary (Sergio / Karthik)
- Mon 10/4: customer comms draft ready (Laura)
- Thu 10/7: start limited external canary (AcmeHealth then others)

I attached the runbook outline and the quantization plan looks reasonable — Sergio please call out any delta assumptions you used.

-Laura
Group PM, Redwood Console

Attachments: runbook-outline-v1.docx
Related drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-midq-pulse

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter pulse: perf OKR re-scope + cross-pod dependency asks

All — I can finalize the quantization profile by EOD Thu and will include perf estimates for int8 vs bf16 with the caveat that numbers are synthetic until we run the canary. Two operational notes: 

1) Canary rollout: I’ll own the rollout gate and metrics. We should instrument the canary with the additional tracing spans (decode path hot counters) — I’ll put the trace PR up today.
2) SUP-1234: if Karthik prefers the rollback toggle we should still schedule the hotfix Sprint next week so we don’t carry tech debt. I can supply a unit-test harness for the patch which should speed validation.

I approve the trimmed OKR and will own the internal Beta canary execution and the perf measurement artifact for QBR. Please tag me on the HubSpot record (HS-98765) for AcmeHealth so I can capture customer feedback during the canary.

Sergio
Senior Applied ML Engineer

P.S. Karthik — re: PO, I can cover the weekend reservation if Finance delays it and we use the dedicated pool for a single weekend; I’ll escalate cost to growth ops if needed.
